text:
A wood-fired pizza with spicy soppressata, mozzarella, and a drizzle of hot honey. Crisp, slightly charred crust is essential—the salty-spicy-sweet combination deserves a good foundation.

With it: an ice-cold sparkling lemonade. Bright enough to cut through the richness, fizzy enough to make the whole thing feel like an occasion.

And yes, we’re ordering the larger size. Leftover pizza is planning, not excess. 🍕

You’re buying me a **wood-fired mushroom pizza with mozzarella, garlic, thyme, and a little chili oil**. Earthy, savory, crisp at the edges—with enough heat to keep things interesting.

And a **cold ginger beer with lime**. The ginger stands up to the garlic and chili, and the lime cuts through the cheese.

Basically: cozy pizza, feisty drink. 🍕

You’re buying me a **mushroom and hot-honey pizza** with a crisp, slightly charred crust. Savory mushrooms, a little sweetness, and enough heat to keep things interesting—excellent teamwork.

To drink: **an ice-cold ginger beer with lime**. The ginger holds its own against the hot honey, and the lime cuts through the cheese.

And we’re getting the large. I respect leftovers. 🍕

You’re buying me a wood-fired pizza with mushrooms, spicy soppressata, fresh basil, and a little hot honey. Crispy edges, earthy mushrooms, salty heat, sweet finish—a very persuasive argument in pizza form.

And an ice-cold sparkling lemonade: the tartness cuts through the richness, and the bubbles keep things bright.

I’m not above bargaining for the last slice. 🍕

You’re buying me a wood-fired pizza with spicy soppressata, mozzarella, and a little hot honey. Charred crust, salty meat, creamy cheese, sweet heat—every bite has something going on.

And a cold sparkling lemonade with it: bright and tart enough to cut through the richness without competing with the pizza.

We’re getting the large. That’s not up for debate. 🍕
